M: Kaldorhold's walls: new stone, no moss yet. Every tenth block is carved with a K.
I: Tall stone houses, all built in the same year, all facing the statues.
5: THE GUT & GAUNTLET. Under the sign, chalked: DAYS WITHOUT A BRAWL: 0. RECORD: 0.
6: THE HALL OF KALDOR. A museum. Of Kaldor. By Kaldor. Free entry. Compulsory entry on Tuesdays.
m: A market stall. The shopkeeper won't take your coin until you've done twenty push-ups. That's the law here.
K: Two statues of Kaldor. The second one is looking up at the first one, admiringly.
q: A barrel. KALDOR'S, it says. Everything here says KALDOR'S.
n: The fist crushing the crown, on a banner so new it still has the fold lines.
c: A lantern on a post, lit. Somebody keeps it burning.
<: The way back west, to the old town.
^: North, toward the shouting of the Training Yard.
>: The east road, toward drums and shouting in time.
_: The south street, toward the smell of ice and old furs.
J: A cocoon in the corner, where nobody looks.
The silk is silver, and very still. You get the feeling it's looking at you.
2: What's left of a wall, black with soot. A building stood here once. A big one.
3: Ash, and a fallen roof beam. Somewhere under it, the ash is still warm. It shouldn't be, after this long.
4: A stone plinth with an empty glass case on it. A brass label, half melted: THE HALE CROWN, AS WORN BY—
The rest has run like candle wax.
0: A notice nailed to a post, in the king's own square hand:
THE MUSEUM OF THE OLD KINGDOM IS CLOSED. THERE IS NO OLD KINGDOM.
STRENGTH CREATES JUSTICE. THE WINNERS DECIDE JUSTICE.

objects.name: Fliss
lines: Kaldor's Sweat! Genuine sweat of the king! Tiny bottles! Makes you strong!
…It's water. It's water from the well. But it's Kaldor's Well, so technically.

answer: Raiders before a fight. Sorrel buys six. She says it's for her knees.
Mott tried to tax it. I gave him a bottle. He's stronger now. Technically.

questions.ask: I can see the bucket you're filling it from.
answer: That's a different bucket. A royal bucket.
…Two for one. Please. Don't tell Mott.

objects.name: Brakka
lines: Furs. Best furs in Kaldorhold. Twenty push-ups and we'll talk.
No push-ups, no furs. I don't make the rules. Well. I made this one. I like it.

questions.ask: Where do the furs come from?
answer: South. Down past the Frost Ward. My cousins trap. I sell. I make you do push-ups.
Elder Skadi says the old Kaldari wore wolves. I say wolves wore them first.

questions.ask: Twenty push-ups? I'll pass on fleas.
answer: Fleas! These furs are clean! I washed them in Fliss's well. Kaldor's Well.
Sixty push-ups now. Price went up. For you.

objects.name: Snik
lines: Sharpening! Axes, swords, spoons, bread, a cat's patience. I sharpen anything.
Brought me a pillow once. Took a week. Very pointy pillow now.

answer: Hroth. Brings the same axe every week. It's sharp. He just likes the chat.
Ansel Chisk brings his chisels. Says Kaldor's nose keeps breaking them. Very hard nose.
Ooh. I'll try. Leave them overnight.
* He holds out his hand for your wits. He's waiting.
…No? Pointy pillow, then. Half price.

objects.name: Ansel Chisk
lines: The king wants another statue. I've done Kaldor standing. Kaldor striding. Kaldor looking at Kaldor.
Kaldor… sitting? Kaldor… thinking? Does he think? I can't ask. You can't ask.

answer: Two hundred and twelve. All Kaldor. Some are the same statue facing the other way.
There's a pigeon on the big one I've grown fond of. It's the only thing in this city not owned by the king.

questions.ask: What happened to the old statues?
answer: Under us. He built Kaldorhold on top of the old city. Old kings, old gods. Buried, standing up.
Dig a well and you hit somebody's marble foot. Fliss's well has a whole marble toe at the bottom.

questions.ask: Your Kaldors all have the same face.
answer: He only has the one face!
…Shh. If he hears 'same face' I'll be doing Kaldor-hitting-a-sculptor next. From life.

objects.name: Mott
lines: Tax collector. Not coin. Fights. Everybody here owes the king fights.
You, for example. Visitor. You owe nothing yet. I've opened a page for you, though. Just in case.

questions.ask: What happens if you don't pay?
answer: The Training Yard. Or the fighters' cells first. Then the yard.
Joss's whole camp owed a tithe. They sent Joss. He writes about clouds. I felt bad. I wrote it down anyway.
Paid? Nobody gets paid. The king pays in honour.
I've got a page for honour. It's empty. Don't tell anyone.

questions.ask: Tax collector? Did your mum know?
answer: She did. She owes three fights. I've got her page right here.
* He writes something on your page. Underlines it twice.

objects.name: Tib
lines: Fight club. Behind the houses. Rule one: tell everyone about fight club.
Rule two: no crying. Rule three: Brunna's not allowed. She bites.

answer: Brunna. She bites. Brunna's not allowed. Brunna keeps coming.
Next week we're doing teams. It's me and a dog against Brunna. I think it's even.

questions.ask: Fight club's just you hitting a fence.
answer: The fence hit me first.
Rule four: no being mean. I just made it. You're out.

lines: THE KALDOR BAZAAR. PUSH-UPS BEFORE PURCHASES.
No haggling. Arm-wrestling only.
THE KING ADMIRES THE KING.
Underneath, scratched small: (so nobody else has to)
Behind the Hall of Kaldor, in a crate marked RETURNS: a Heart Piece.
Somebody tried to sell it at the bazaar. Nobody could do enough push-ups.

objects.name: Oona
lines: * She steps out of the silk, a silver blindfold over her eyes, and turns her face straight to you.
There you are. You were later than I saw. Only a little.
The future is shy. Be patient with it.
Tomorrow it will rain in Warrior City. Bring a cloak. That is all I am going to tell you, and it is quite enough.
* Oona walks away along the wall without once touching it.

objects.name: Sir Gaudry Plume
lines: Mind the robe. It's woven from the beards of defeated men. Fourteen beards. Very itchy. Very expensive.
My grandson's a champion. So I live here, by the Hall of Kaldor, where the roads are paved and the rain is warmer.

answer: Exhausting. Every morning I must choose which of my eleven gold spoons to be disappointed in.
And everybody's trying to rob me. Yesterday the butler. Today the second butler. Strong lads. I may hire them back.
The king's quarter gets the good weather. I don't know how. I don't ask.
In the old town the rain's cold and sideways. That's what you get for weak children.

questions.ask: Your spoons can't fight for you.
answer: Spoons can't, no. But I can buy a man who can, and he can buy a spoon.
* He tucks all eleven spoons into his robe, and watches you very carefully.

objects.name: Old Vessant
lines: Gaudry's spoons. Gaudry's beard robe. Gaudry, Gaudry, Gaudry.
I have a solid gold chair. Gold is very cold, and very hard, and very mine.

questions.ask: How did you get so rich?
answer: Four sons. All champions. The king pays a champion's family like a small country.
The fifth went north, to the camp. We don't say his name. Well. I say it at night, sometimes, when nobody's listening.
…Don't tell Gaudry.
Everyone. This is Kaldorhold. Your neighbour waves at you in the morning, and by teatime he's measuring your door.
So I sleep in the chair. It's very hard to steal a gold chair while somebody's sitting on it.

questions.ask: Bit sad, sleeping in a gold chair.
answer: SAD? It's GOLD.
* He sniffs. His teeth chatter, ever so slightly. Gold is very cold.

objects.name: Primrose Varley
lines: Don't block my view. Champion Vorn's flexing. He does it at eleven every morning. I've been here since six.
Oh, you're nobody. Never mind. Stand there if you like. You're practically see-through.

answer: He came out of the culling games top of his year, and he still has both his ears.
Marry a champion, bear a champion, and they treat you like a goddess. Statues. Chairs carried about. People bow at your soup.
It's better than love. It's a plan.
Love doesn't come with a house by the king.
He noticed me on Thursday! He sneezed in my direction.
* She takes out a little handkerchief, which she has clearly kept since Thursday.

objects.name: Champion Vorn
lines: * He flexes. Somewhere behind you, Primrose sighs.
The culling games, the year I turned eighteen. Eleven went in. I came out. That's maths.

questions.ask: What happened to the other ten?
answer: Didn't make it. That's what the games are for, small one. Only the strongest go on.
Now I live by the king, and I'm to father as many children as I like. Strong ones. The kingdom needs them, the king says. I've nine.
The march. The wizard kingdom. Any day now, the king says. We take it, like the island.
Five hundred of us took the island in one day. I wasn't born yet. I'm still cross about it.
Everyone watches me. Odessa, Brisa, a horse in Warrior City. It's a lot of watching.
…Who's Primrose?
…Strong. Little Strong. Strong Two. Big Strong.
* He counts on his fingers, gets to five, and starts flexing instead.

objects.name: Dame Gisela
lines: Kneel, if you like. Most people kneel. I've had three champions. The city's very grateful.
They built a statue of me. Then a bigger one. Then they ran out of marble and did my feet in gold.

questions.ask: What's it like, being treated like a goddess?
answer: Lovely. People carry me about. I haven't walked since the second champion.
My legs have forgotten how. I don't mind. Somebody else's legs are always nearby.
…I had three champions.
* She says it again, more firmly, as if the number might change if she doesn't.

questions.ask: You didn't do any of the fighting.
answer: No. I did the being-born-from. Try it sometime. See which you prefer.
* She waves a hand, and somebody nearby fans her, very hard, in your direction.

objects.name: Krag
lines: * He's tied a rope round his arm and is pulling it tighter, to make the arm look bigger. His hand has gone purple.
Champions have big arms. I'll have big arms. Even if I lose the hand.

answer: Loosen? Loose is weak. Weak goes north.
…It's tingling. Tingling's strength leaving. Or arriving. One of those.

questions.ask: Why do you want to be a champion?
answer: Kaldorhold's cutthroat. Everybody's out for everybody. My landlord pushed me down the stairs last week, to see if I'd bounce.
Champions don't get pushed down stairs. Champions own the stairs.

questions.ask: Your hand's going to fall off.
answer: Then I'll have one very strong arm. That's still one more than most.
* He pulls the rope tighter, out of spite.
